mutations.name: the original defect — deletion-only accounting, so a length-increasing rewrite of caller content stays silent
the count threshold rises past the reported two-occurrence case, so the SQL-DDL rewrite goes back to being silent

SURVIVOR (documented): the growth branch drops its `re.global` condition. Harmless TODAY, and the premise is asserted by the 'no non-global rule carries a capture group' test rather than left implicit. String.match(nonGlobalRe) returns [fullMatch, ...captureGroups], so the count can only exceed 1 for a non-global rule that HAS a group — and none does, so with MULTI_HIT_REWRITE_WARN_COUNT=1 every non-global rule yields hits=1 and `1 > 1` is false either way. NOT dead code: it is what stops a spurious warning the moment someone adds a capture group to a non-global rule, which is a normal thing to do when a replacement needs $1. If that premise test ever fails, this mutation must be re-run — it becomes load-bearing and should then be CAUGHT.
the two branches stop being exclusive, so a large deletion is ALSO reported as a rewrite
the over-deletion branch loses its threshold, so the W2 guard it was built for reports every deletion
OVER-REACH CONTROL: the count threshold drops to zero, so every global rule warns on every single hit including the trigger the rule exists for
